headline: JISDOR sets another record at 18,278 and the JCI falls a fifth day, so the 1Y adds 7.2bp and the 10Y closes at 7.751%, a new high that trips the underweight rule by 0.07bp, even as Treasuries rallied 3bp; the daily flow signal holds at −0.85
summary: The front end kept repricing BI: the 1Y rose 7.2bp to 6.870% (+7.9bp this week), the 2Y 4.8bp to 7.077% and the 3Y 3.7bp to 7.289%, while the 5Y added 2.7bp to 7.603%, the top of 17 stored days and +13.4bp this week. The 10Y rose 1.2bp to 7.751%, the highest on the dashboard's history since Nov 2021 (+12.3bp this month), and the 15–30Y 1.1bp to 7.754%; with the front leading, 1s2s narrowed 2.3bp to 20.7bp and 2s5s 2.1bp to 52.6bp, still the 94th percentile of 17 days. The 1Y now sits 87.0bp over the 6.00% BI-Rate, from 79.8bp. FR0109 lost 4.0bp to 7.568% (4.5bp cheap) and PBS040 2.9bp to 7.557% (13.0bp cheap), while the fitted PBS 5Y moved to 4.8bp through IGSYC, retail is 12.0bp rich at 5Y and AAA 3Y is 49.2bp over, mid-range for 16 stored days.
drivers: The rupiah set another record and the front end priced more BI

JISDOR fixed at 18,278, a fresh record and 0.05% weaker on the day (0.33% this week, 0.77% this month), and spot closed 0.09% weaker at 18,270, its weakest close on record (Kontan); analysts tied it to a firm dollar near 103.8 and bets on a December Fed hike. Two days after BI's hike the 1Y rose 7.2bp and the 2Y 4.8bp, so the 1Y−BI-Rate gap widened to 87.0bp, still the 18th percentile of 17 stored days (average 102.6bp). I read that as the market adding to the odds of another BI move while the rupiah keeps sliding; BI has not committed to a level.
Stocks fell a fifth day with heavier foreign selling

The JCI lost 0.92% to 5,146.33, touching 5,094.89 intraday, with foreign net selling of Rp947.41bn (Katadata), up from Rp563.6bn on Thursday; Bloomberg Technoz puts foreign net equity selling above Rp100tn this year. Over 20 sessions the JCI is down 15.55%, the signal's most bearish input after the 10Y trend. Who traded bonds today is not published, so any link from equity selling to INDOGB selling is a hypothesis.
Treasuries rallied again; INDOGBs did not follow

The US 10Y fell about 3bp to 5.04% on Thursday as jobless claims (203k vs 197k expected) and a weak Philly Fed (6.3 vs 20.0) met a sell-off in US stocks. At the 1-year daily beta of 0.29 that implies −0.9bp for the INDOGB 10Y; it rose 1.2bp, so Treasuries explain none of today's move. The INDOGB − UST spread widened to 271.1bp from 266.9bp, the 92nd percentile of 52 weeks (range 191–300bp), a nominal pick-up before currency risk.
A much smaller current-account deficit did not help the rupiah

BI reported a Q3 current-account deficit of $2.0bn (0.5% of GDP) against $12.6bn (3.4%) in Q2, and a balance-of-payments surplus of $0.1bn, on a wider non-oil trade surplus and lower energy imports. But the portfolio account stayed in deficit as foreign buying of domestic debt slowed, which the market weighed more than the trade side; BI's quarterly figures do not rule out bond selling since September.

BI-Rate 6.00%, +25bp; DF 5.25%, LF 6.75% (f split: 10 of 27 for a hike, rest hold; p 5.75%)
1Y +8.9bp a day later and +7.2bp today; JISDOR at records since.
FOMC minutes, Oct 27–28 meeting (Nov 18)
Almost all saw further hikes as likely; a couple open to >25bp in Dec (f hawkish lean, p held 3.75–4.00%, 10–2)
CME pricing about 97% for a 25bp December hike (Gate/CME).
BI capital flows, Q4 to Nov 16 (Nov 18)
Portfolio +$4.8bn; equities −$0.9bn (f n/a, p n/a)
Inflows led by global bond/sukuk issuance and SBN; equities still leaking.
SBSN auction (Nov 17)
Bids Rp20.10tn, awarded Rp10tn; SPNS Rp6.90tn of it, PBS041 at 7.09% (f target Rp10tn, p bids Rp28.56tn)
Demand skewed to short bills; long PBS bids selective.
SUN auction (Nov 10)
Bids Rp79.71tn (p Rp31.09tn); awarded Rp35tn vs Rp30tn target; FR0110 7.44%, FR0111 7.68%
Strong demand at higher yields; the next SUN book is the first test after the hike.
view: The hike still has not turned the rupiah (JISDOR at a record 18,278) and the 10Y closed at 7.751%, 0.07bp over my 7.75% trigger with the daily signal below −0.5, so the underweight rule is on, but I run it small because the signal's sell-off calls have had little edge. The daily Bond Flow Signal is −0.85 (also −0.85 on Thursday on today's rebuild): the 10Y trend part is the most bearish (z +1.66, +50.2bp over 20 sessions), then the JCI (z −1.57, −15.55%) and the rupiah (z +1.12, +2.54%), while the spread, 25.8bp above its 130-day average (z +0.93), leans bond-bullish; the sell-off episode runs from Sep 30 (26 sessions, +63.3bp). Since July 2022 the daily signal scores a Sharpe of 0.67 outright (178.3bp) and 0.77 hedged against Treasuries (201.7bp), against −48.2bp for holding the 10Y, but sell-off calls were right only 53% of the time over the next 20 sessions (hedged 52.6%; rally calls 58%, hedged 64.5%) and the 10Y actually fell 0.2bp on average after them; on the same daily build the outright Sharpe was 1.02 in Jul 2022–Aug 2024 and 0.43 since. The weekly build scores 0.44 and 0.54 and its signal is −0.16 (neutral); a variant using the US 10Y trend reaches 0.89 and 0.91 on the weekly build but was chosen after the fact and is not live, and all of these are in-sample back-tests. Over four weeks the INDOGB 10Y is up 29.3bp and the US 10Y 8bp, yet at the weekly beta of −0.21 the Treasury-linked part is −1.7bp and +31.1bp is residual, the part Treasuries do not explain. I expect the 10Y in 7.65–7.90%, keep the 5Y as the curve trade (buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70%, 3.2bp away) and see the 1–2Y as the bucket most exposed to a December hike.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The 1Y rose 7.2bp to 6.870%, so the gap over the 6.00% BI-Rate widened to 87.0bp from 79.8bp, still the 18th percentile of 17 stored days (average 102.6bp); the 2Y is 7.077%, 107.7bp over. The 3M (0.25Y) is 6.27% and the 1M 6.14%, 14bp over the policy rate. The 7.00% add level was not reached (1Y 13bp away); no position.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y at 1Y 7.00%, target 6.75%, stop 7.25%; unchanged, since the 1Y is still inside its stored average gap to the policy rate.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109 / PBS040)
buckets.why: The IGSYC 5Y rose 2.7bp to 7.603%, the top of 17 stored days (100th percentile, average 7.508%), +13.4bp this week; the 2s5s10s fly is 37.9bp (82nd percentile, average 27.6bp). FR0109 lost 4.0bp to 7.568% and cheapened to 4.5bp over the curve from 3.6bp, so the entry (7.60–7.70%) is 3.2bp away and not filled.
buckets.call: Keep: buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70%; target 7.35%, stop 7.95%. The curve point is the cheapest stored; the bond is moving toward the entry.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The IGSYC 10Y rose 1.2bp to 7.751%, a fresh top of the stored history since Nov 2021 (100th percentile of 1,118 days, average 6.79%), against a 3bp US rally; +12.3bp this month. With the signal at −0.85 and a close above 7.75% by 0.07bp, the pre-set underweight rule triggered. FR0108 rose 1.3bp to 7.749%, on the curve.
buckets.call: New: small underweight from 7.75%, target 7.95%, stop 7.62%; size it small because sell-off calls hit only 53%. Cover if the signal rises above −0.5 or JISDOR falls below 18,000.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC 10s20s is 0.3bp (24th percentile of 17 stored days, average 1.3bp, range 0.1–2.9bp); the long end is flat. The benchmark spread FR0107 − FR0108 is 0.5bp (from 0.7bp), 5.5bp from the −5bp re-entry.
buckets.call: Wait. Re-enter the FR0108/FR0107 steepener duration-weighted at −5bp or lower, target +5bp, stop −12bp.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.why: The fitted PBS 5Y moved to 4.8bp through IGSYC from 0.1bp (19th percentile of 16 stored days, average −1.6bp), mostly because PBS030 rallied 9.3bp to 6.913% as the FR front end sold off; the fit rests on four series (level −4.9bp, slope 0.4bp), so confidence is limited. PBS040, held from 7.52%, is 7.557%, 3.7bp against, and 13.0bp cheap to the curve. PBS034 rose 0.8bp to 7.647% and is 5.9bp rich (from 5.3bp), a small further loss on the FR-over-PBS034 switch; its 10bp stop was not hit.
buckets.call: Hold PBS040 from 7.52%: target 7.30%, stop 7.80%. Hold FR over PBS034: close if PBS034 is more than 10bp rich to IGSYC; switch back once it is 5bp cheap (10.9bp away).

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y rose 4.4bp to 7.781%, a touch more than IGSYC, so the spread is 49.2bp (44th percentile of 16 stored days, average 49.9bp), off Thursday's low of 48.5bp. AA is 87.5bp over (average 86.9bp), A 154.5bp and BBB 231.7bp over AA (+8.6bp; 44th percentile, average 236.2bp). Sixteen days is a thin base and PHEI's corporate curves track IGSYC almost one-for-one; the add level (AAA 3Y past 70bp) was not reached.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB while funding costs rise with the BI-Rate.

buckets.name: Retail SBN 5Y (ORI/SR)
buckets.why: The fitted retail curve is 12.0bp through IGSYC at 5Y (62nd percentile of 16 stored days, average −13.4bp) and on the curve at 2Y (−0.1bp); the fit uses 26 series with a 45bp slope, so part of this is fit artefact. Secondary spreads run from 48bp rich (SR024T3) to 68bp cheap (ORI027T3, 7.695%); ORI026T6 is 7.706%, 33bp over. ST017 (open to Dec 2) floors at 6.95% (2Y) and 7.05% (4Y), now below the IGSYC 2Y (7.08%).
buckets.call: New money: FR0109 or PBS040 for liquidity; ST017 only for hold-to-maturity buyers who want further BI-hike upside. Buy secondary retail only at the cheap end (ORI026T6, ~33bp over).

watch: Next: the next SUN auction (one of two left this year) as the first test of demand after the hike, US markets shut for Thanksgiving on Thu Nov 26, MSCI deletions at the Nov 30 close, Indonesia's November CPI on Dec 1, the ST017 book closing Dec 2, the Fed decision on Dec 9 and FTSE deletions on Dec 21; a 10Y close below 7.62% would stop the new underweight, while JISDOR back below 18,000 would argue against a December BI hike.
